scope: Shared typed service/companion projection and app-owned queued delivery; live legacy iOS watch wiring; native source reuse; common protobuf level adapter; watch arithmetic fixes and retained-watch CI build. Production native iOS root/writer/background adoption is not activated.

productionLines.scope: Physical lines in app-owned tracked/new App/**/*.swift and Shared/Sources/**/*.swift; excludes Pods, Tests, AppTests, AppStoreScreenshots, FontScreenshotter and the two owner-only annotated files. Includes all changed production files, not merely deleted/moved ones. Test, resource and documentation lines are reported separately, not hidden as production Swift.

lineCountMeaning: Production Swift grows 97 physical lines (30,119 to 30,216), including touched legacy-controller formatting. WatchHelper shrinks 201 to 145 and legacy Home 345 to 331, with one common level adapter; this is not a net LOC reduction.

nativeMac.reason: The runner failed to initialize UI automation before the app launched. This is not a passing UI check or a diagnosed product defect.

invariants: Watch transport accepts only typed projections, with all eight legacy packet fields/types preserved and the send timestamp appended at transfer.

The shared sender keeps only the latest absolute schedule while unavailable, recomputes counts/bins at activation and consumes the duplicate window only after an accepted send. Typed equality preserves changed-data and clock-rollback behavior.

Source reads are separate from system notification I/O. Denied/disabled notification choices and blocked notification status cannot delay a valid companion clear; stale reads and failed/unconfigured sources never publish fabricated new progress.

Vacation clears review forecasts while retaining known level progress; logout queues empty account data. Valid higher-level fallback preserves the existing half-level convention without a fabricated level 0.5.

Legacy Home and service projection share one protobuf level-progress initializer. Native availability supplies the same service type while retaining native visibility/access/pending/exclusion/kana rules.
The watch timeline horizon uses hourly units capped at 24 hours and empty progress rings produce a finite zero fraction. No watch UI redesign or modern widget replacement is claimed.
UI fixtures inject both notification and companion operations. No real watch session, notification prompt, app badge change or live WaniKani exercise is part of the selected UI acceptance.

simulatorInterruptedRun.reason: A run overlapping hosted tests ended with a bootstrap SIGKILL and failed simctl diagnostics; an isolated rerun passed all 419. The cause is unproven; no product workaround or disabled check was introduced.

validationLimits.physical: Builds and synthetic source/sender tests do not prove paired-device transfer, actual permissions, signed upgrades or physical speech/IME behavior.
validationLimits.legacy: The WatchKit/ClockKit UI, character placeholder, watch branding/resources and modern widget replacement remain open. Native iOS companion/background composition and root/writer cutover still require the remaining parity work.
validationLimits.diagnostics: Mac Release has zero reported warnings; iOS/watch retain legacy framework/protobuf warnings. These are incremental diagnostics, not whole-project warning-elimination evidence.
validationLimits.CI: Workflow syntax and the once-per-iPhone-matrix retained-watch command are validated locally; no hosted Actions pass, tool publication, signing/store distribution, PR or push is claimed.

rootAndMainboard: No parent manifest, Mainboard implementation or unrelated owner sources were edited or staged.
